Consonantal i

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

along preposition and adverb

following the length of: along the river, along the road

also alongside

classical

Plaut. Rud. 148–149: quid illūc est … hominum secundum lītus?
Cic. Att. 16.8.2: iter secundum mare superum faciunt

secundum (+ accusative)

preposition with the accusative

along, alongside (a river, a coast, a road)

Following the line of a thing, beside it: secundum flūmen, along the river; secundum lītus, along the shore. Its other senses, after and in keeping with: see according to.

Other words

  • viā, lītore (ablative alone) — along (the way one goes)

    ablative of the way, without a preposition · also used · classical · Hor. S. 1.9.1: ībam forte viā Sacrā

    The road one goes by stands in the ablative: viā Sacrā īre, go along the Sacred Way (see via). Per viam, through the street, is also said.

  • praeter (+ accusative) — along, past

    preposition with the accusative · also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.48.2: praeter castra Caesaris suās cōpiās trādūxit

    Along and past a thing: see past.

Examples

  • Prō dī immortālēs, quid illūc est, Scēparniō, hominum secundum lītus?

    Good heavens, Sceparnio, who are those people over there along the shore?Plaut. Rud. 148–149

  • hieme cum hībernant secundum mare, aestū abiguntur in montēs frondōsōs

    in winter they winter along the sea; in the heat they are driven up into the leafy mountainsVarr. RR 2.5.11

  • an īret ad trīs legiōnēs Macedonicās quae iter secundum mare superum faciunt

    or whether to go to the three Macedonian legions that are marching along the Adriatic coastCic. Att. 16.8.2

  • ībam forte viā Sacrā, sīcut meus est mōs, nescio quid meditāns nūgārum, tōtus in illīs

    I happened to be walking along the Sacred Way, as is my habit, thinking over some trifle or other, quite lost in itHor. S. 1.9.1–2

See also next to, past, via, according to.
